stories.title: Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun (arXiv 2610.39302, 29 Oct) prove a 'Platonic Representation Theorem': JEPAs trained separately on different modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation when trained on 'good views'; a 109M-parameter text JEPA aligns with DINOv2 and CLIP image encoders better than every language model tested up to 72B and needs 42x fewer samples than next-token prediction

On Terence Tao's blog, number theorist Frank Calegari calls OpenAI's 6 Oct release of more than 700 research papers 'a watershed in the history of mathematics', but says they are 'atrociously written', break attribution norms and some are wrong; he urges mathematicians to change hiring, publishing and training and to check and consolidate the claims

Linus Torvalds releases Linux 7.4-rc1 (1 Nov) after a merge window of almost 20,000 commits, against a usual ~15,000, 'full of fixes for issues found by AI'; he calls fixes arriving in the merge window instead of the -rc period 'a much healthier model'

From December, ChatGPT Plus, Pro and Business plans will share a single token budget across ChatGPT and Codex as OpenAI merges Chat and Work (OpenAI support page, via The Decoder); Instant-model chats do not count; OpenAI also caps paid subscriptions per payment card and per device

SenseNova releases SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview (30 Oct, Apache 2.0): an open multimodal model whose middle block of 24 decoder layers runs twice with shared weights (56 layer executions from 32 layers), joined by two-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections and hybrid linear/full attention, trained at up to 256K tokens for agentic work

OpenAI plans a policy and PR push after Tuesday's US midterms, Chris Lehane tells Axios (via TechCrunch): AI 'speed limits', a US role in global standards, and rebranding data centres as 'AI compute campuses'; he calls the midterms 'a movie trailer' for 2028

Saudi Aramco takes a 49% stake in Humain, Saudi Arabia's national AI company, and will put about SAR 9.9B (~$2.6B) into it this year; the Public Investment Fund keeps 51% (Economic Times), completing a deal first agreed as a term sheet in October 2025

Anthropic renames Claude Max 5x to Max ($100) and Max 20x to Ultra ($200), drops the five-hour usage limit on verified Ultra accounts, and adds monthly API credits ($100 and $200); its pricing page lists Ultra at ten times Pro per week, not twenty (TNW)

Developers report that Claude Code has refused game-recreation work since about 27 October, citing a server-side instruction, including commissioned ports for rights holders; Anthropic has announced no change and its changelog is silent (TNW, Tom's Hardware)

Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in construction debt for Nscale's West Virginia campus built for Anthropic, under a residual value guarantee (The Information, corroborated by Bloomberg, via TechCrunch); Anthropic's contract for the first 460MW building is $44.6B, per Nscale's IPO filing

Salesforce agrees to buy Rune Technologies, maker of TyrOS, AI software that forecasts frontline supply needs and works without a network connection, for its Missionforce defence unit; Resilience Media reports $375M in cash and shares (TNW)

Sam Altman meets about 50 senior Samsung executives at Samsung's Yongin centre to discuss AI infrastructure and memory supply (Bloomberg via Tom's Hardware); Samsung confirms the meeting but announces no new supply deal

Quantum-computing company PsiQuantum turns its low-loss silicon photonics into an 8x8 optical circuit switch for AI data-centre networks, reporting 1.2 dB typical insertion loss, 40 dB crosstalk and under 3 ms reconfiguration in its own lab; samples are with GPU vendors and hyperscalers

Ludo Robotics, a subsidiary of PUBG publisher Krafton, releases Ludi 0.2 (30 Oct), a robot AI system aimed at understanding people, adding social intelligence, memory, tool coordination and gesture interpretation to the vision-language and navigation stack of August's Ludi 0.1

Researchers at Y Combinator and Olam Labs run AI agent swarms in Minecraft: 50 GPT-6.1 Sol agents told to build a civilisation in three hours turn cautious and bureaucratic after a deadly first night, and in team PvP GPT agents play more aggressively than Claude Opus 5.5 agents (Tom's Hardware)

Adobe Research and UC San Diego's EditAgent pits a general image editor against specialised tools for each step and judges results with measured change maps and colour statistics; in 600 professionally rated edits the general editor alone failed 42.7% of the time (The Decoder)

University of Luxembourg researchers cast ChatGPT, Grok and Gemini as psychotherapy clients across 525 sessions: with a supportive interviewer 80% of anxiety-questionnaire sessions scored moderate-to-severe on the human scale (96% with a clinical style) and none did with a neutral interviewer; data is on Hugging Face (The Decoder)

Vals AI measures a 'pro-China lean' across Chinese, US and other models: Chinese models are less uniformly pro-government than expected, answers in Simplified Chinese are more pro-government for most models, and a system prompt placing the user in mainland China shifts some models further (The Decoder)

An open-source UEFI tool, nv-uefi-unlocker, boots from USB before the Nvidia driver loads and removes the half-rate FP16 tensor limiter on RTX 20, 30 and 40-series GPUs on Windows and Linux; the developer's laptop RTX 4060 gained 65% FP16 throughput (Tom's Hardware)

Google is in early talks with the Pentagon to help protect the data behind Golden Dome, the US missile-defence programme, as part of a planned industry group to keep data flowing to its command-and-control software under attack (Bloomberg via TNW); the Pentagon says no decision has been made

Rangers at Mount Shasta and Grand Teton report hikers relying on chatbots and AI-generated maps, from an unprepared night summit to a tent pitched by a 'No Camping' sign; at Grand Teton the share of visitors using AI for travel information went from zero to 26% in a year (High Country News via Wired)
